author: NewsBreak
title: Missing from Norfolk, Nebraska since 1987, a female child was never found - NewsBreak
text:
3 hours ago Jillian Dee Cutshall. Photo by NCMEC website. Jillian Dee Cutshall would be 47 now if she were still alive. She has been missing from Norfolk, Nebraska, since August 14, 1987, at age 9. She was last seen walking to her babysitter's home around 6:30 a.m. and it was reported she was sitting on the steps at the babysitter's house.
Jillian's parents divorced in 1985. Jillian and her brother lived with their mother, Joyce Cutshall, in Great Bend, Kansas. Joyce later remarried. Jillian was staying with her father and stepmother for the summer in 1987, at an apartment building in Norfolk, Nebraska.
The National Center for Missing and Exploited Children (NCMEC) provided the above age-progressed photo to 34 years (on the right). When Jillian disappeared, she had pierced ears and a scar on her right upper lip. She also had a two-inch vertical scar on the crown of her head, according to The Charley Project . Because Jillian has never found, it's hard to talk about her in the past tense.
For additional images, visit The Resource Center for Cold Case Missing Children's Cases or The Charley Project. Jillian has blonde hair and blue eyes, and she also goes by "Jill."
Reportedly, Jillian didn't like being in the apartment alone, so she was going to walk to her babysitter's house. Some resources indicate she never arrived to her babysitter's house and it's also been stated that she was sitting on the steps at the house. One resource indicated she was sitting on the stoop waiting for her babysitter to wake up, and yet another, stated if the babysitter wasn't there, a hidden key was available for Jillian to use.
Regardless, she never arrived inside the babysitter's house and the babysitter wasn't aware she was there waiting. It wasn't discovered that Jillian was missing until after 3:00 p.m. when her stepmother went to pick her up. The babysitter assumed Jillian had decided to stay at her father's home and had not come over since she didn't arrive.
Three months after Jillian disappeared, her keys, clothing, and shoes were found at the Wood Duck Wildlife Refuge in Stanton, Nebraska (Stanton County) by a hunter. The location is 10 miles from where Jillian's father lived.
On a tip, Jillian's mother was led to David C. Phelps in 1988. Interestingly, that tip came from Phelps' sister who was a journalism student at the same local college Joyce Cutshall was attending.
It's been stated Phelps lived with Kermit Baumgartner in the same apartment complex as Jillian's father during the summer of 1987. Because Phelps had met Jillian, he was interviewed twice by the police in 1988. Baumgartner was also interviewed and he moved out of the apartment after that.
During the second interview with Phelps, he said that since his teens, he had been molesting children. His preference was for girls between the ages of 4 and 6. He described six incidents, which charges were never filed. He had indicated that Jillian was too old for his liking.
In early 1989, Jillian's mother hired a private investigator who drove Phelps to the wildlife refuge where Jillian's clothing were found. The private investigator later divulged his own secret of having served time before for burglary and having a false detective license. But he also indicated that he was also driven to find Jillian for her mother.
Phelps gave the private investigator a statement that he and Kermit Baumgartner, who also had a record for sexual assault, had taken Jillian to the wildlife refuge.
Phelps was able to describe the clothing. He also indicated he became nervous during the incident, leaving Baumgartner alone with Jillian in the refuge. Baumgartner had allegedly told him to take the car and drive back home.
Phelps said he never saw the child again. Baumgartner denied having anything to do with Jillian's disappearance. He also was never charged.
The private investigator also had a television crew from Omaha record the interview which was reportedly shown later on 60 Minutes possibly in 1991.
When the police interviewed Phelps, he recanted his earlier statements saying that he was coerced by the private investigator who also had a gun he shot up into the air. (See the summary of Phelps' appeal , State v. Phelps , 490 N.W.2d 676 (1992); 241 Neb. 707.)
Initially, neither men were ever charged. Baumgartner eventually left for California and Phelps moved to Iowa. Jillian's mother, Joyce, who was on a mission to find answers, started a petition for a grand jury to open an investigation. She was successful in obtaining more than enough signatures.
The Madison County grand jury indicted Phelps for abduction with the intent to commit sexual assault. Phelps was reported as a longtime suspect when he was arrested in Perry, Iowa.
While Jillian’s mother was almost 100% sure her daughter was no longer alive, she was hoping that the indictment and trial would further the investigation into where her daughter was.
In the spring of 1991, Phelps was convicted to life in prison without the possibility of parole. Since Jillian's remains were never found, Phelps wasn't convicted of murder .
His conviction and sentence were affirmed by the Nebraska Supreme Court, see State v. Phelps, 490 N.W.2d 676 (Neb. 1998) (“ Phelps I”), and several subsequent motions for post-conviction relief have been denied. ( Source : Phelps v. Frakes, Memorandum & Order, Case No. 8:14CV151.) In 2022, Joyce Jean Storovich Cutshall Mosley died at age 68. Her obituary published in the Norfolk Daily News , noting she had remarried and that she was predeceased by her daughter, Jillian.
To date, no one has been charged with causing Jillian's death. After Phelp's conviction, Jillian was declared legally deceased. She has never been located.
If you have any information, contact the Norfolk Police Department in Nebraska at 1-402-644-8700. You can also reach out to NCMEC's 24/7 call center at 1-800-843-5678, and reference case/file no. 600904.
Thanks for reading and sharing.
